title: The Eagle and the Cocks
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: There were two Cocks in the same farmyard, and they fought to decide who should be master. When the fight was over, the beaten one went and hid himself in a dark corner; while the victor flew up on to the roof of the stables and crowed lustily. But an Eagle espied him from high up in the sky, and swooped down and carried him off. Forthwith the other Cock came out of his corner and ruled the roost without a rival. Pride comes before a fall.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the two Cocks fight?
options: To decide who should be master
To win the favor of the farmer
To protect the farmyard from a fox
To settle a dispute over food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the beaten Cock do after the fight?
options: He challenged the victor to a rematch
He hid himself in a dark corner
He left the farmyard entirely
He crowed loudly in defiance

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the victorious Cock do after winning the fight?
options: He flew up to the roof of the stables and crowed lustily
He went looking for the beaten Cock
He rested quietly in the farmyard
He immediately left to find food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the victorious Cock while he was on the roof?
options: He fell off and injured himself
An Eagle spotted him and carried him off
He was chased away by a farmer
He challenged another rival to fight

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the beaten Cock do once the victor was carried off?
options: He fled the farmyard in fear of the Eagle
He came out of his corner and ruled the roost without a rival
He challenged the Eagle to a fight
He hid even more deeply out of fear

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "espied" mean in "an Eagle espied him from high up in the sky"?
options: Ignored
Spotted
Followed
Warned

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did crowing lustily on the roof put the victorious Cock in danger?
options: It drew the Eagle's attention by making him visible and conspicuous
It startled the beaten Cock into attacking him from behind
It used up his strength so he could not fly away
It alerted the farmer, who then removed him from the roof

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the closing line, "Pride comes before a fall"?
options: Eagles are the natural enemies of all farmyard birds
Boastful display after a victory can expose one to a danger that ends the triumph
It is always better to lose a fight than to win one
Farmyards are dangerous places for any bird to live

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the beaten Cock hide after losing?
options: In a dark corner
On the stable roof
Behind a haystack
Under the farmhouse porch

questions.prompt: According to the passage, from where did the Eagle spot the victorious Cock?
options: From a nearby tree
From high up in the sky
From the farmyard fence
From inside the stables

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the beaten Cock end up doing after the Eagle takes the victor?
options: He rules the roost without a rival
He is also carried off by the Eagle
He challenges the farmer for control
He leaves the farmyard for good

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "lustily" mean in "crowed lustily"?
options: Vigorously and loudly
Softly and briefly
Nervously and quietly
Slowly and sadly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what allowed the beaten Cock to end up ruling the farmyard in the end?
options: The Eagle's unexpected removal of his rival, not any effort of his own
His decision to challenge the Eagle directly
A truce he negotiated with the victorious Cock
His own crowing, which impressed the farmer

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: After winning a fight, one Cock boastfully crows on a rooftop and is carried off by an Eagle, leaving the beaten Cock to rule alone
Two Cocks join forces to defeat an Eagle together
An Eagle mediates a fight between two Cocks
The beaten Cock is carried off by the Eagle instead of the victor
